notes: Two concurrent GitHub Copilot REPL sessions launched in the SAME cwd (driver start_session step; both slots share RUN_CWD). Each launch mints its own $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<uuid>/ directory, so the SESSIONS never collide — only the PID binding is at risk, because copilot/pid.go is DiscoverPIDByCWD and both processes cwd-match. The claim-aware disambiguator (PIDManager.claimAwareDisambiguate: highest UNCLAIMED candidate) is what keeps them apart, the same path session_detector_pid_test.go pins adaptor-agnostically. EVERY phase anchors on a WORKING transition, never a ready: copilot is a presession adapter (the process exists while its session dir still holds only workspace.yaml), so up to TWO born-ready proc-<PID> placeholders are in flight here and a ready-anchored new_session phase would greedily bind to one. proc-* rows never enter working. Copilot mints its own UUID per launch, so the two distinct session ids are asserted relationally (new_session / same_session_as), not literally. Assertions: (1) session 1 does an independent working->ready turn; (2) a DISTINCT session (s2_turn1_start carries new_session:true) does its own working->ready turn; (3) session 1 is driven AGAIN while session 2 is alive (s1_turn2_*, pinned same_session_as s1_turn1_start), proving its PID-to-session binding stayed stable and never flapped to session 2. Phase order follows the recipe: s1 turn -> start_session -> s2 turn -> s1 turn again. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map, so both are asserted non-zero; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn — nondeterministic across three turns.
